paper_id: TransLinkGuard_ Safeguarding Transformer Models Against Model Stealing in Edge Deployment
title: TransLinkGuard: Safeguarding Transformer Models Against Model Stealing in Edge Deployment
motivation: Edge-deployed LLMs become white-box accessible, enabling model stealing; existing PTSE defenses fail to balance security and efficiency
problem_framing: Four properties must be simultaneously satisfied: proactivity, request-level authorization, runtime security, and negligible overhead
key_insight: Avoid direct TEE computation entirely—use permutation matrices to disrupt positional info, authorization only rearranges features (lightweight)
method_signature: Weight permutation + TEE-based OTP-encrypted authorization with MLP integration across all transformer layers
evaluation_criteria: MS attack accuracy (security), TEE FLOPs ratio (efficiency), accuracy preservation vs original model
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: FLOPs metric is platform-irrelevant; no systematic hardware overhead evaluation across diverse environments
evidence_for_taste: shielding entire LLMs within TEEs results in a roughly 50× reduction
offload a significant number of layers to GPUs
probability of guessing the correct π is 1/(d!)
attacker must approximate a substantial portion of the parameters
thinking_moves: 识别PTSE方案的根本弱点是直接执行模式，而非试图改进其参数分配策略
从对称加密(OTP)获得启发，将其用于授权过程的信息隐藏
将授权机制集成到MLP块中，使第二个线性层参与授权，从而增加参数复杂度抵御逼近攻击
